crash: Handle new warning format The kernel has switched its warning format to include CPU and PID in the WARNING line per [1] which landed in the 3.11 cycle. Kernels 3.10 and earlier continue to use the old format. Adjust the analyzer to understand both old and new format. Also update the test to use a warning message in new format for testing most edge case behavior, but keep a copy of the old format and make sure it still gets picked up by the collector. [1] https://kernel.googlesource.com/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/+/dcb6b45254e2281b6f99ea7f2d51343954aa3ba8 BUG=chromium:668134 TEST=FEATURES=test emerge-$BOARD -v1 crash-reporter Change-Id: I41617d1a112170961d198625caba58d35a5ef385 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/414905 Commit-Ready: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org> Tested-by: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

libcontainer: fork/exec setfiles only once for faster ARC boot Previously, run_setfiles_command() which spawns /sbin/setfiles was called for each mount_external mount point and because of that, labeling files and directories took 800-900ms on Cyan. With this CL, /sbin/setfiles is called only once, and the time will be like ~150ms. BUG=b:33348324 TEST=ARC still starts Change-Id: I2fa97cfb1d5920ef7fadbb3f289530baeb8bb2e4 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/416394 Commit-Ready: Yusuke Sato <yusukes@chromium.org> Tested-by: Yusuke Sato <yusukes@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org>

libcontainer: do not run setfiles for /cache Just like /data, which libcontainer already skips, Android's /init.rc will label files and directories in /cache right after the container starts. Removing this redundant setfiles scan makes ARC faster to boot. BUG=b:33348324 TEST=Start ARC, run "find /run/containers/android_*/root/cache -exec ls -Z {} \; | sort" with and without this CL, confirm the results are the same. Change-Id: Idf09c0304b3733d35febf698b1fc78756d6b0447 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/416395 Commit-Ready: Yusuke Sato <yusukes@chromium.org> Tested-by: Yusuke Sato <yusukes@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Luis Hector Chavez <lhchavez@chromium.org>

goofy: make goofy use test_list_iterator Goofy is now using new test_list_iterator to maintain test list running state. The following features / APIs are no longer required / provided anymore. * UpdateSkippedTests: the run_if function is now evaluated when a test gets a chance to run, so we don't need to call this function to update skipping status of tests when device data is changed. * starting_at: the "starting_at" argument was provided by auto_run and other similar functions. This argument made Goofy start running from a given test and continue all the following tests, which is different from providing a "root", and only run tests under this node. Currently, we don't see any requirement for this feature. To simplify the implementation of TestListIterator, this feature is now removed. Can add it back when we find this feature is useful. * backgroundable and force_background: These test attributes were made to allow tests running in parallel. However, these would increase unnecessary complexity to test list execution logic. We provide a new attribute "parallel" to FactoryTest, which means that all subtests of this test should be run in parallel. login: Emit login-prompt-visible Upstart signal async. Make session_manager's D-Bus method call to Upstart to emit the login-prompt-visible signal be asynchronous. This is a speculative fix for cases where session_manager appears to block on this call, possibly due to other Upstart jobs hanging at startup. Continue to use synchronous requests for all other Upstart signals. I'm also updating systemd to support starting units asynchronously, although I'm unsure of whether those D-Bus calls to systemd are ever expected to block. BUG=chromium:671662 TEST=unit tests pass; also deployed to a samus device, ran "initctl log-priority info", and verified that that emit-login-prompt is still emitted and that boot and login appears to work as before Change-Id: I661a9dc03c2430622a85ce4d51c47ce22ed5d63e Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/417181 Commit-Ready: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Tested-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org>

shill: fix kDefaultLeaseExpirationTime definition |kDefaultLeaseExpirationTime| in ipconfig.cc is supposed to be the maximum value of `time_t`. This CL changes the code to use std::numeric_limits<time_t>::max() to obtain the maximum value of `time_t` instead of std::numeric_limits<long>::max() as the latter assumes `time_t` is defined as `long`. The change also indirectly fixes the following cpplint warning: Use int16/int64/etc, rather than the C type long [runtime/int] BUG=None TEST=Run unit tests.
